input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.2 imposes a one-way liquidated exit charge payable solely by the Company (our client) whenever it terminates: 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, paid in eight quarterly instalments. HDI never owes a reciprocal amount (4.2(b) expressly confirms it makes no payment even if the formula is negative). The charge is untethered from the fees actually payable (30% of Net Sales over $11,000/month) and is triggered by any Company termination — including the 90-day non-renewal right in 4.1 and termination for HDI's breach — so it can exceed remaining contract value on a one-year rolling term. That contravenes the playbook position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by the Customer. Redline deletes Section 4.2 and conforms the Section 4 heading; the fallback offer is a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees for convenience terminations only.

proposal.summary: Delete the Company-payable Termination Payment in Section 4.2 and conform the Section 4 heading.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the Termination Payment, which is a liquidated exit charge payable only by us (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales over $800,000) and is triggered by any Company termination, including termination for HDI's own default; our position is that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by the Company. If an exit fee is essential, we can accept a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees, payable only where we terminate for convenience.
